source.title: FDA Approves Once-Weekly Generic Hormone Therapy Patch for Women

sentences.sentence: The US FDA approved the first generic version of the Climara Pro once-weekly patch, which combines estradiol and levonorgestrel, on 20 October 2026.
The US FDA approved the first generic of Climara Pro on 20 October 2026.
Climara Pro is a once-weekly patch containing estradiol and levonorgestrel for women with an intact uterus.
The FDA describes the generic as therapeutically equivalent to the brand product.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.
On 20 October 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the first generic version of Climara Pro.
Climara Pro is a transdermal patch, worn for a week at a time, that contains estradiol and levonorgestrel and is for women with an intact uterus.
The FDA describes the generic as therapeutically equivalent to the brand product.
The FDA says the progestogen in the patch is there to reduce the risk of endometrial hyperplasia, which can occur with oestrogen alone.
The agency presented the approval as a way to widen access to more affordable medicines.
This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: An extra year of secondary school lowered dementia diagnoses later in life

sentences.sentence: An NIH-funded study reports that one extra year of secondary school in the UK was linked to fewer dementia diagnoses later in life, mostly in people at higher genetic risk.
An NIH news release dated 23 October 2026 describes an NIH-funded study of schooling and dementia.
The study used a UK reform that raised the minimum school-leaving age by one year.
It reports fewer dementia diagnoses later in life, with the largest effect among people at higher genetic risk.
This is research news from a US agency, not UK guidance.
A US National Institutes of Health (NIH) news release dated 23 October 2026 describes a study that found an extra year of secondary school was associated with fewer dementia diagnoses later in life.
The NIH funded the study, which was led by researchers at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Southern California.
The researchers analysed a UK education reform that raised the minimum school-leaving age by one year, treating it as a natural experiment.
The release says the effect was largest among people at higher genetic risk of dementia.

The researchers estimated a reduction of 0.88 percentage points in Alzheimer's disease and related dementia over 50 years, which the release calls sizeable given how low overall dementia rates were in the study population.
They said the effect may change as the group ages and diagnoses become more common.
This is research news from a US agency; it does not change UK guidance.

source.title: FDA approves zidesamtinib for ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer

sentences.sentence: The US FDA approved zidesamtinib (Jideytro) on 22 July 2026 for adults with previously treated ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer.
The US FDA approved zidesamtinib (Jideytro, Nuvalent) on 22 July 2026.
It is for adults with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer who have had at least one ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor.
The approval rests on a single-arm, open-label trial called ARROS-1.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.
On 22 July 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved zidesamtinib (Jideytro, Nuvalent).
It is approved for adults with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer who have already received at least one ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor.
The FDA says the approval rests on ARROS-1, a single-arm, open-label trial.
It reviewed the application under its Real-Time Oncology Review pilot programme and acted two months before its goal date; the medicine holds orphan drug designation.

The label lists warnings for central nervous system adverse reactions, QTc interval prolongation, interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis, skeletal fractures, and muscle pain with raised creatine phosphokinase.
This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.
